title: Friday the 13th
build: G64 disk image: a one-line loader, a title program that loads at $2900, a 29,299-byte main program at $5800, two data files at $0C00 and $E000, and a 880-byte program at $0400. One sector on the disk has a bad checksum

entry of the main program: points the STOP-key vector $0328 at $940F so RUN/STOP is never seen, resets the stack, prints $8E (upper-case set) and $08 (case switching off) through CHROUT, sets the player's state $0918 to $FF (no round played yet), and falls into new_game

start of a game after a death or when time runs out: sets the text screen up, clears the counsellor index $09EE and rounds won $09EF; if a round was played ($0918 not $FF) it prints the death message (text 0, player state 0) or the time-out message (text 1), the score and PRESS FIRE; then clears the six score digits $08DC-$08E1 and prints the title text 2, then goes on at choose_counsellor

Jason is dead: prints text 3 (congratulations), counts the counsellors still alive (state not 0 in $090E-$0917), adds 100 points for each with ten calls of add_score (A is ten times the count, which add_score hands back unchanged; with no one alive each call adds 256 points), puts the count as a digit in the two bonus lines on the text screen ($54F4, $5506), adds one to rounds won $09EF, and moves on to the next counsellor in $09EE (0 to 4, then back to 0)

prints the profile of counsellor $09EE (text 4 to 8), sets the player's sprite pointer $0820 from $9414, the player's strength $0943 from $941E and colour $09F0 from $9423, puts the player's sprite in the middle of the profile, clears the ten scare flags $09F1, waits for fire, silences voices 2 and 3 for the random generator, copies this counsellor's 11-byte weapon list from $9A41 (offset from $9A78) to $A5AA, and starts play at start_play

stops any tune (stop_music), blanks the screen ($D011 bits 4 and 5 cleared), banks BASIC out, points the interrupt at $9398, turns off every sprite, sets all sprites to multicolour with colours 6 and 10, selects video bank 1 with the screen at $5400 and the ROM font copied to $4000 (copy_rom_font), clears the screen, sets a purple border on black, multicolour text off, and turns the screen on: the text screens use this
interrupt used on the text screens: reads the keyboard and joystick (read_input) and leaves through the KERNAL's own handler at $EA31
prints PRESS FIRE BUTTON. ($9A22) on line 23 with PLOT and CHROUT, then waits for the fire flag $0824 to show fire up and then down: $0824 is 1 while fire is released

prints text number A from the block at $9428, whose texts end in $FF: texts 0 to 3 clear the screen first (CHR$ 147), texts 4 to 8 (the profiles) start at row 14 column 12 with PLOT. Counts past A terminators, then sends each byte to CHROUT
the routine RUN/STOP checks go to: LDA #$FF, CMP #$7F and RTS leave the zero flag clear, so the key is never seen as pressed
sprite pointer of each counsellor in play, by counsellor 0 to 4 (Gerry, Wendy, Amanda, Bryan, Stuart): $6D for the men, $88 for the two women Wendy and Amanda

fear value of each counsellor: Gerry 4, Wendy 7, Amanda 9, Bryan 5, Stuart 7; the player's fear rises by it when Jason attacks a friend, and by twice it on seeing a body (scare_check); the profiles' "hidden weakness"
starting strength of each counsellor, copied to $0943: Gerry 75, Wendy 35, Amanda 45, Bryan 50, Stuart 70; Jason's blows take it down
sprite colour of each counsellor (7 yellow or 2 red); the bytes from $9428 are the start of text 0
the nine texts print_text prints, each ended by $FF. Text 0 (death) starts here with eight cursor-downs, colour $98 and "OH DEAR ....!"
the rest of text 0, the death message: YOU SEEM TO HAVE LOST YOUR HEAD. WHAT A SHAME......HA HA HA, then the score line
text 1: OH DEAR ....! YOU RAN OUT OF TIME BEFORE YOU FOUND HIM, then the score line
text 2: the title screen, FRIDAY THE 13TH and the question that opens the introduction
text 3: CONGRATULATIONS ! JASON IS DEAD.....BUT FOR HOW LONG ? and the two bonus lines round_won fills in
text 4: GERRY KING's profile, printed under his portrait
text 5: WENDY WATSON's profile
text 6: AMANDA BAXTER's profile
text 7: BRYAN BONE's profile
text 8: STUART PALMER's profile
PRESS FIRE BUTTON. after a $9E colour code, ended by $FF, printed by print_press_fire
the $FF that ends PRESS FIRE BUTTON.

which object type each of the 11 objects is when this counsellor picks it up, 11 bytes for each counsellor; a counsellor who cannot use an object finds it as another type. Gerry gets 0 to 10 in order; the others lose some (Wendy has a second type 0 where 6 should be)
where each counsellor's 11 bytes start in counsellor_weapons: 0, 11, 22, 33 and 44

sets the play screen up: banks BASIC out, points the interrupt at irq_play ($A71B) with a raster split, selects bank 1 with the bitmap at $4000 and screen at $5400, multicolour on with background 11, 10 and 6, empties the held weapon $08CE and the 11 object rooms $097B, sets the player's state $0918 to 4 and the danger clock $0821 to 0, then puts the 11 objects in random rooms 0 to 43 (each a different room, never the player's), each on a random tile 0 to 31 ($0986)
picks which of the ten other counsellors Jason is disguised as: a random number 0 to 9 into $0992

picks the room that object 10 lives in: a random room 24 to 43 that no other object uses, into $0985; object 10's tile is 19 ($0990). Then puts the player at column 0 row 1 of area 2, sets up the actors (init_actors) and draws the first room
prints SCORE : and WEAPON : ($A5B9, in the panel's own letters) on row 17 with PLOT and CHROUT, then draws the rest of the panel (draw_panel)

one pass of the game: waits for the interrupt's flag $09B7 to clear (the raster is in the panel), redraws the room if the player changed room ($08EC), then multiplexes up to four people onto sprites 0 to 3, nearest the bottom first, from the four slots $099F-$09B6 that update_actors filled

takes the slot with the smallest y left in $09BF, works out its screen position and collision with the room (place_in_room), writes the sprite's position, priority, pointer and colour; the player's own slot (number 0 in $09AB) also sets the player's sprite bit masks $08CC and $08CD and copies its position back

rest of the pass: restarts the theme tune if the interrupt is not the music's, ends the game if the player is dead ($0918 = 0), ends the round if Jason is dead (round_won), waits for frames, runs the throw, then on every other pass (half_pass) counts pass_count, tries jason_reveal every 256 counts, checks the shelter and raises the danger clock by 2 every 128 counts (at $C0 the time is up), reads sprite collisions and moves the counsellors (update_actors), then reads the stick for the player

turns the stick into the player's movement: a hurt player ($0918 bits 6 and 7) shows the hurt frame; no stick shows the standing frame facing left or right; otherwise steps the walking frame counter $08C8 (0 to 4) and the 4-step counter $08CA, moves the player (move_room in an outdoor area 0, the room's edges in a building), and plays the footstep (silent, at $C1F2)
for actor slot X: sets $08D3 to 1 for another actor, 0 for the player, then goes on as place_sprite

finds the two tiles under the feet of the person at $08BA (x) and $08BB (y) in the room's 8x4 tile map $0894: the tile columns are 32 pixels wide and the rows 32 high, so $08BD and $08BE are the tiles under the left and right foot and $08BF and $08C0 the ones below; tests each with tile_kind to stop a walk into a solid tile, to climb a step up or down by 2 pixels, or to take a door (door_check), and returns the sprite's screen x in X, y in Y and its x high bit in A

moves the player one room in an outdoor area: adds the stick's step $08B4 to the column $086A and $08B6 to the row $086B, holding each inside the area's width and height ($A58C and $A58D), then works out the room number (room_number)

room number of the current place: base room of the area $08B9 ($A5B5) plus row times the area's width plus column, into $086C; packs area, column and row into one byte (area times 64, column times 8, row) in $08EC and $090D, draws the room and starts the tune that belongs there

a chance that Jason, still disguised as counsellor $0992, starts killing: none if he already has; the chance is a random number below the danger clock $0821 plus 20 falling under $0821, so it grows as time passes. Sets his state to 7, picks his victim $0993 (the counsellor with the highest exposure $092E other than Jason and those sheltering, the dead included, or the player if the player's fear $0938 is higher than all of them), and plays tune 4

draws the current room: sprites off, a scare check (scare_check), the backdrop (draw_backdrop), then the room's 32 tiles from $0C00 plus room times 32, 8 across and 4 down; each tile is 4 by 4 cells from $8000 plus tile times 32 (two bytes per cell, a cell number drawn by draw_cell), coloured from $A5DA; copies the tiles into $0894 for collisions; marks the safe room if this is $0985, then shows any object that lies here
after drawing: clears the step tiles $81-$84 from the collision map (clear_steps), hides the object sprites 6 and 7, then looks for an object whose room ($097B) is this one

places object Y in the room: moves its tile down to the nearest empty tile (0), and in a building onto one of the floor tiles listed at $A665; turns the tile into a position and shows it on sprite 7 with its pointer ($A59F) and colour ($A594) for the type the counsellor sees it as

the player is at a doorway: in a building (area 1, 2 or 3) tile $54, $02 or $56 is the way out, to one of the three door places ($BB2E) in the outdoor area 0; outdoors tile $2C, $20 or $36 leads into building 1, 2 or 3, which start at column 0 row 0. Sets the new area and place, draws it and repositions the player
flashes the border for 160 frames by counting the interrupt's frame counter $08C7
width and height in rooms of each area, two bytes each: area 0 (outdoors) 4 by 6, area 1 3 by 4, area 2 2 by 2, area 3 2 by 2; 44 rooms in all
height half of each area_size entry, read as $A58D plus twice the area
sprite colour of each object type 0 to 10: all 1, white
sprite pointer of each object type 0 to 10 ($E4 to $FE in steps of 2); the second of each pair is the weapon flying the other way
this counsellor's 11 object types, copied from counsellor_weapons when the round starts
first room number of each area: 0, 24, 36 and 40
SCORE : and WEAPON : in the panel's letters (@ABCD and EDFGBH), ended by $FF
colour of each tile, by tile number 0 to $8A: low nibble for colour RAM, high nibble for the screen byte, the two multicolour pairs the tile's cells use
the 18 tiles an object may be put on in a building
the four frames of a walk cycle, 0 1 2 1, added to the walking person's first sprite pointer
reads the whole keyboard into $082A (read_keyboard) and then the joystick (read_stick)

scans the 8 by 8 key matrix: drives each $DC00 row low in turn and stores one byte per key at $082A + row times 8 + 7 minus bit, 1 if the key is down; the BIT $01A9 at $A6A1 hides an LDA #$01 that the pressed path jumps into

turns keys and the joystick into movement: two pairs of keys give $0826 (left -1, right +1) and $0827 (up -1, down +1), one key gives the fire flag $0824 (1 while released) and another $0828; then the joystick in port 2 ($DC00) replaces them whenever it is pushed or fired

the play screen's raster interrupt, called twice a frame. At line $B2, under the play area, it turns bitmap mode off for the panel, sets the background black and moves sprite 6 to the panel's weapon box showing the held weapon ($08CE), and asks for the next interrupt at line 256. At line 256 it turns bitmap mode back on, sets the play area's background $08DA, adds one to the frame counter $08C7, sets $09B7, puts sprite 6 back, reads the keyboard and stick, clears the hit flags (clear_hits) and leaves through $EA81

draws one 8 by 8 multicolour cell into the bitmap at $4000 + 8 times the cell position: the cell's 8 bytes come from $1180 + 8 times the cell number held in $09DF (high) and A (low); pixel pairs of %00 are see-through, so the cell is masked onto what is there. Then sets the colour nibbles of the cell's screen byte at $5400 from the tile's colour $0872 (outdoors, both nibbles)
the operand of the LDA at $A859, written by draw_cell before each cell: the address of the cell's 8 bytes

high byte of cell_source's operand ($11 plus the cell number's high part), then the masking loop: each non-zero byte of the cell is laid over the bitmap so that its %00 pixel pairs let the room show through; then the cell's screen byte at $5400 takes the tile's colours (in a building only the low nibble changes, outdoors both), and $08C7 is set to 2
copies the panel's letters into the character set (copy_panel_letters), fills the bitmap $4000-$53FF with $AA and clears the screen bytes $5400-$567F, the play area's 16 rows

outdoors (area 0), clears the play area's 16 rows of bitmap and sets a grey background; in a building, draws the room's perspective walls and floor from the one picture in RM, the same for every building room: a 16 by 32 map of cells at $0400, each map byte's low five bits a pattern, from $0700 when bit 5 is set and $0600 when it is clear; then colours it from two bytes per room at $AA5E (room minus 24): the background and three colours, chosen per cell by the map byte's top two bits
with the I/O banked out, copies the character ROM's first 2 KB ($D000-$D7FF) to $4000-$47FF, the font the text screens use
copies 240 bytes from $3260 into the panel's character set at $59E8, characters 61 to 90: the panel's figures and letters
the four colours draw_backdrop gives the map's top-two-bit values, written for each room
third of the four backdrop colours (high nibble of the room's second byte)
fourth of the four backdrop colours (low nibble of the room's second byte)
two bytes for each building room (rooms 24 to 43): background in the high nibble of the first, then three colours in the remaining nibbles
second byte of each room_colours pair, read as $AA5F plus twice the room
moves the player in a building room, the 3D view (sets $AEB4 to 0, then shared with walk_actor)

moves a person inside a perspective room: adds the step to $08BA and $08BB, then keeps the person inside the floor, whose half-width shrinks with depth ($AEB7, one value for each 6 pixels of y); a step through the back wall or the front edge leaves the room through a door when the room has one on that side
after a room change, puts the person at the opposite edge of the floor: the same side mirrored about x $74, or y flipped with EOR #$60
the step at the back or front edge of the floor: checks for the doorway (door_edge), then for an actor moves x towards the middle by 4 or 8
is the person in the doorway, x between $6C and $7B? the player at column 0 row 0 and near the back may go out; otherwise the step across the edge is cancelled
for an actor walking along the back or front edge, moves y by 2 or 4 back onto the floor
a person standing on stairs (stairs_tiles) is moved up or down them; otherwise an actor at a blocked edge turns
looks at the four tiles under and beside the person ($08BD to $08C0) for one of the 15 stair and slope tiles at $AEC7, and moves the person 2 pixels up or down it, or 4 pixels sideways off it
an actor blocked vertically picks a new direction from its turn state $0965 and the step table $BB3A
sets the vertical step $099A from the stick's y, or 1 when there is none

what a tile is to someone walking: one of the five tiles at $AEAF (steps and ladders) returns carry set, A 0; tiles below $19 are open (carry clear, A 0); tiles $19 to $37 are solid (carry set, A 1); tiles from $38 are open
the five tiles that tile_kind treats as climbable: $0F, $12, $15, $17 and $45
0 when walk_player moves the player, 1 when walk_actor moves another counsellor
which depth band of the floor the walker is in, kept from the last check
the walker's vertical step, kept across walk_actor
half the floor's width at each depth, one value for each 6 pixels down: $74 at the back down to $38 at the front, in steps of 4
the 15 tiles stairs_tiles looks for; $FF is an empty slot
first sprite pointer of each look a counsellor can have, 0 to 3 from the low two bits of $BB88, and 4 for Jason unmasked
sprite pointer of each look lying dead
0 or 5: picks the right-facing or left-facing frames

sets the ten other counsellors up at the round's start: each at x $54, y $31, wandering (state 4), at a start place from $BB7E, with a random exposure $092E of 10 to 74 and strength $0939 of 20 to 59; sets the sprite pointers of sprites 1 to 7 to $0B and the frame counter $099D; then falls into update_actors

moves the ten other counsellors once (frame_tail calls it every other pass) and fills the four sprite slots with the ones in the player's room. For each counsellor (index in $0991, 9 down to 0): a sheltering one (state 5) counts down $095A every 16 counts of pass_count, adding a point to the score, until it walks home; a wandering one (4 to 7) heads for its target place $0903, through a door of its building when the target is in another area

the counsellor's step for this pass in X ($0995 holds y): sets the walking frame, then moves it within the room (walk_actor in a building, an edge wrap outdoors) and, when it crosses the room's edge, to the next room (actor_next_room)

if the counsellor is in the player's room and a sprite slot is free (up to 2 for friends, every slot for Jason), fills the next slot $099F-$09B6 with its x, y, frame (dead, walking or Jason's), step and number

Jason hunts (jason_hunt); a counsellor that has reached its target walks on to a new random target in its area, chosen with the turn table $BB42 and its turn count $0923; one at a door of its building comes out at the door's place outdoors, or in at the building's first room
the x and y step of turn direction A from $BB3A: returns x in A and y in Y
sets voices 3's frequency high byte and control to $80 (noise) so its oscillator gives random numbers, then falls into random
a random number from 0 to A minus 1: the raster line's low bit ORed with voice 3's noise ($D41B), reduced by subtracting A until it is below A
moves the counsellor in X one room by $099B and $099C, held inside its area's width and height, and stores the new packed place in $08E2

for sprite A, which other sprite is touching it: none ($FF) if the hardware collision byte $08C6 does not have its bit; otherwise the one whose bit is the only other one, or the nearest within 24 pixels across and 21 down
waits for the play interrupt's flag, sets $08D0 so the panel shows no weapon icon, does the action (use_weapon), waits again and clears the flag

fire with the stick still picks up, swaps or drops a weapon; fire while moving throws it (throw_weapon). Holding object 10 outdoors does nothing. A free object on the player's sprite is picked up into $08CE; one already held is put down on the tile under the player, or swapped for the one touched
the player touched an object while holding one: swaps their rooms and tiles, so the held one is left where the other was
puts the held object down in this room at the player's tile and hides the panel icon; with object 7's slot, moves sprite 6's object to sprite 7

Jason (state 7) after his victim $0993: if they are in another room he heads for it; if the victim shelters (state 5) he gives up and goes home, and a counsellor victim also makes him give up unless a random number below 60 is under its exposure; otherwise the victim panics (state 8), every counsellor's exposure goes up by 2 and the player's fear by the fear value of the counsellor the player is; when Jason is within 13 pixels across and 4 down he swings (jason_swing)
sends counsellor X back to its start place wandering (state 4), with 3 more strength (at most 80)
fire while moving: if nothing is flying and a weapon is held, sets the throw's direction $09C5 from the facing and starts the weapon's flight (weapon_anim) on sprite 4

sets the frames of a weapon's flight or swing from its type $09D7: types 0 to 2 fly (3 frames, kind 3), 3 to 6 swing (kind 2), 7 and up a long swing (kind 1); sprite pointer and colour from $A59F and $A594
moves the thrown weapon on sprite 4 each pass: 4 pixels a pass across the screen until it leaves at x below $20 or $38, then lands it in the room (land_weapon); a swing counts down its frames
the weapon stops: sprite 4 off, the held weapon goes back to the floor (the player keeps it), and the hit flags are cleared (clear_player_hits)
draws the weapon held out from the player in each frame of a swing, offset by the table at $BB0E, on sprite 4
steps the frames of a swing of kind 1 or 2
steps the frames of a throw (kind 3)
x and y offset of the weapon from its holder for each frame, two bytes each, facing left then right
y offset half of each weapon_offsets pair
the place outdoors that each building's door leads to, as a packed place, for buildings 1 to 3 (entry 0 unused)
the bits 1, 2, 4 to 128, one per sprite
x and y step of each of the four turn directions, two bytes each
y step half of each turn_steps pair
60 turns a wandering counsellor makes, read 10 at a time from a random row
the packed start place of each of the ten other counsellors
each counsellor's look: high nibble its sprite colour, low two bits its sprite set, low nibble its picture in the panel
the frame shown for each frame of a hit counsellor
a work byte shared by several routines (a loop counter, a cell offset)

the flying weapon on sprite 4 hits a counsellor: takes the weapon's damage ($BC57) off its strength $0939; at below zero it dies (state $40, a scream). If it was Jason, the player scores the weapon's points ($BC61) and Jason, if still alive, unmasks (state $47) and turns on the player; hitting an innocent friend costs 2 on the danger clock
sprite_hit with Jason's weapon sprite 5 left out of the collision byte
strength taken from a counsellor by each object type 0 to 7: 6, 6, 6, 2, 2, 3, 2, 8
strength Jason's blow takes ($BC5F = 8), plus the rounds won
points (tens) for hitting Jason with each object type 0 to 9: 60, 60, 60, 10, 10, 15, 10, 120, 120, 120
starts or steps Jason's blow on sprite 5: from the direction of his victim, a long swing (type 8), drawn while he is in the player's room

when the blow touches its victim (the player if Jason is in the player's room and his sprite hits theirs): takes Jason's damage plus rounds won off the victim's strength; below zero it dies (state $80, a scream)

once the player has been in the safe room this round ($09ED) and object 10 still lies there ($0985 not $FF, else shelter_end): a counsellor the player's sprite touches, in any room, alive, not Jason and not sheltering, goes to shelter (state 5) with the safe room as its target, for 90 minus its exposure in shelter_time; its exposure rises by 2 if the player holds an object
with no safe room (object 10 carried, $0985 = $FF), every sheltering counsellor goes back to its start place and wanders again
redraws the room map for the counsellor's room and runs place_sprite for it, keeping its x, y and steps
copies the 32 tiles of the room at packed place A into $0894 (room number from area, column and row, as room_number) and clears its step tiles
turns tiles $81 to $84 in the room map $0894 into open floor (0)

at line 256 each frame: clears the "hit by the player" bit $40 of every counsellor when no weapon flies, and the "hit by Jason" bit $80 when he is not swinging; forgets Jason's victim when Jason is not hunting; sends a panicking counsellor (state 8) that is not the victim back home

draws the panel's fixed parts into the screen at $5400 and colour RAM: the fear head (16 characters from $10), the strength box (characters from $31), the dividers ($0A and $0B), and the ten counsellor boxes (from $21)
writes a block of characters, 4 across, rising by one, with colour $0822, 6 rows down
draws the ten counsellors' pictures in the panel: alive, each in its colour (from $BB88) and picture; dead (state below 3), the body picture $55 in brown
one counsellor's picture, 2 characters across and 3 down, at the place $C210 gives
writes 3 characters across, X rows down, with colour $0822
redraws the fear head, the danger bar, the strength meter, the counsellors and the score
copies one of 8 pictures of the head (128 bytes each from $2D80) into the panel's characters at $5880, chosen by the fear $0938 divided by 10
draws the danger clock $0821 as a bar in the panel's characters at $5988, one column of pixels for each 2
masks for an odd last column of the danger bar
offsets of the 8 head pictures from $2D80, 128 bytes apart
head_offsets read from the second entry on
the footstep sound, switched off: an RTS stands in front of a routine that would set the volume and play a short noise on voice 1
screen offset of each of the ten counsellor pictures in the panel

in a building room on the building's outer edge, covers the doorway on that side: the side wall's door in the first column (edge_left) and the last (edge_right), the back wall in the top row (edge_top), the bottom row (edge_bottom); outdoors draw_backdrop returns before calling it
covers the back wall's doorway in a room on the building's top row: 4 rows of $55 in the bitmap
the same for a room on the building's bottom row
covers the left wall's door in a room in the building's first column, from the patterns at $0730, 12 cells down
ORs one 8-byte pattern from $0730 into the bitmap
covers the right wall's door in a room in the building's last column, the left patterns mirrored pixel pair by pixel pair
ORs one pattern from $0730 into the bitmap, mirrored
the patterns that cover the right wall's door
the patterns that cover the left wall's door
blanks the panel to the background colour, waits for the interrupt, plays the sampled scream (play_scream), then clears the panel and redraws it
writes the six score digits from $08DC and a final 0 into the panel's screen at $56B5, in colour 3
one score digit plus the character offset $0A20
adds A points to the score by calling add_one A times; a stored point shows as 10 on the screen
adds one to the six decimal digits $08DC-$08E1, carrying; past 999999 the score goes back to 0
clears the "hit by the player" bit $40 of every counsellor
draws the player's strength $0943 as the weights on the bar in the panel: picks a 32-byte slice of the picture at $3180 by strength divided by 4, into the characters at $5908
copies 4 by 8 bytes of the strength picture, from the slice the strength picks in $3180-$3217, into $09FB-$0A1A

starts tune A: saves the interrupt vector and points it at irq_music, sets the tempo ($C8DB) and repeat flag ($C8E2), finds the three voices' note lists inside the tune (each ended by $FF) from the tune's address ($C8CD), sets the SID's first note of each and starts
interrupt while a tune plays: at line 256 counts down the tempo and steps the tune (music_tick) before the play interrupt's own work; at line $B2 goes straight to the play interrupt

reloads the tempo counter and steps each voice: a voice's counter ($0800-$0802) reaching zero gates the note off and reads the next pair (note, length); a note of $80 or more is a command ($C78A), $FF ends the voice. When all three voices end the tune repeats or the old interrupt comes back
SID frequency of note A: 12 notes of the top octave from $C874, halved once for each octave below; returns high in X, low in A
runs tune command A (0 to 3) through the table at $C88C by pushing its address and returning into it

the tune commands 1 to 3, each taking the byte after it (left in the voice's length counter $0800-$0802) and then skipping on (tune_skip): this one, command 1, sets the voice's waveform byte $0803-$0805
command 2: writes the byte to the voice's attack and decay register ($D405 plus the voice's offset)
command 3: writes the byte to the voice's sustain and release register ($D406 plus the voice's offset)
command 0: turns the tune's repeat flag $0812 on and skips only the command, so the next byte is read as a note or command
starts the tune again from its saved voice addresses
moves a voice's pointer on by the command's length
swaps the six zero-page pointers $FB-$FE and $8B-$8C with the music's copies at $0813-$0818, and switches the KERNAL out (the tunes lie under it at $E000) or back in
SID frequencies of the 12 notes of the top octave, high byte first
addresses minus one of the four tune commands, in command order 0 to 3: repeat on ($C7CF), waveform ($C7A4), attack and decay ($C7AF), sustain and release ($C7BF)
sets the music's pointers to a silent tune and waits until the interrupt is no longer irq_music
a voice script that rests for one step and ends ($00 $01 $FF): stop_music points all three voices at it
where each of the 7 tunes starts, all under the KERNAL: $E000, $E4F6, $E628, $EA12, $EB98, $EC63, $EDC9
frames between steps of each tune
1 if the tune repeats: only tune 0, the theme

the player walks into a room where a counsellor lies dead: the first time, a 1 in 5 chance (a random number 40 to 49 of 0 to 49) adds twice the counsellor's fear value to $0938 (at most 80) and shows a full-screen picture of the body with a scream
with the KERNAL banked out, draws one of two pictures (a random choice) from under the KERNAL: a 16 by 32 map of cells from $F000 or $F930 with its cells, and colours
operand of the LDA at $C9C2, written by show_gore for each cell: the picture's base ($0A1E) plus $0200 plus 8 times the cell number; the loop copies the cell's 8 bytes into the bitmap
high byte of gore_cell_source's operand; the copy loop then steps through the 16 rows of the picture's map
copies the picture's colours to the screen at $5404 and fills colour RAM with one colour
starts the tune of a place: if the packed place $08EC is one of the six at $CA6B and the last tune started was the theme ($0819 = 0), starts tune 1 to 6
the six packed places that have a tune of their own
tune 0, the theme, the one that repeats: five SID register bytes for each voice, then each voice's script of (note, length) pairs, commands from $80, ended by $FF
tune 0, continued
tune 1, played at one of the six places in tune_places
tune 2, played at a place
tune 3, played at a place
tune 4, the one that plays when Jason reveals himself and at a place
tune 5, played at a place
tune 6, played at a place; the tunes end at $EF02
the first gore picture, drawn on half the screens with a body: a 16 by 32 map, one byte per cell, each a cell number 0 to 165 whose 8 bytes lie at $F200 plus 8 times the number
the first picture's 166 cells, 8 bytes each: cells 0 to 127
the first picture's cells 128 to 165
the first picture's screen colours, 16 rows of 32; colour RAM is filled with 9
the second gore picture, drawn on the other half: its 16 by 32 map, one byte per cell, cell numbers 0 to 37 from $FB30
